entities.name: Prostate carcinoma
observations: Preoperative mp-MRI has limited sensitivity for pathologic extracapsular extension, seminal-vesicle invasion, overall T3 disease, and pelvic lymph-node metastases, despite generally high specificity.
mp-MRI is best interpreted as complementary to clinical risk assessment, biopsy findings, nomograms, and selected PSMA-PET rather than as a stand-alone staging test.

entities.name: mpMRI local staging
observations: A 2016 meta-analysis of 75 studies and 9,796 patients found sensitivity/specificity of 57%/91% for ECE, 58%/96% for SVI, and 61%/88% for overall T3 disease against prostatectomy pathology.
The authors characterized MRI as high-specificity but poor and heterogeneous-sensitivity staging, with only modest improvement from 3-T imaging and functional sequences.

entities.name: mpMRI routine staging
observations: A 2023 institutional and Pennsylvania regional study found sensitivity of only 2.9%-49.2% institutionally and 16.8%-24.4% regionally across pT2N0, ECE, SVI, nodal, and bladder-neck endpoints, while specificity was 89.1%-100% and 93.9%-98.6%.
The investigators advised against using mp-MRI as the sole staging method in routine practice.

entities.name: mpMRI nodal staging
observations: A 2021 meta-analysis of 9 studies and 640 patients found mp-MRI sensitivity 0.40, specificity 0.92, and AUC 0.82 for pelvic lymph-node metastases against lymph-node dissection.
The low sensitivity means a negative mp-MRI cannot reliably exclude nodal disease.

entities.name: mpMRI SVI detection
observations: In a 2024 multicenter cohort of 528 prostatectomy patients, MRI sensitivity for pathologic SVI was 0.162 and specificity was 0.963.
MRI-positive SVI was relatively credible, but MRI missed most pathologic SVI.

entities.name: mpMRI T-stage agreement
observations: A 2023 multicenter study found exact MRI-to-pathology T-stage agreement in 71.2% of cases.
Poor-quality scans (PI-QUAL <3) had more pathologic upstaging than higher-quality scans (35% vs 19%; OR 3.4, p=0.01).

entities.name: mpMRI clinical impact
observations: A randomized 438-patient trial found no significant overall reduction in positive margins with preoperative MRI (19% vs 23%, p=0.4).

A 2023 propensity-weighted cohort of 1,259 prostatectomy patients found no significant mpMRI-versus-CT differences in positive margins, biochemical-recurrence-free survival, complications, or one-year functional outcomes.
